correctness.rationale: Checked exact x-quadratic discriminant λ²y²(1-y²/3)²+4(8/3-y²). Its unique upper turn lies in (sqrt(8/3),sqrt3), from strict derivative negativity on y² in (8/3,3). The chord area must integrate to moving Yλ, not the λ=0 circle radius. The large-λ proof splits at both zeros of h=y(1-y²/3); local models y and 2(sqrt3-y), with q(0)=32/3 and q(sqrt3)=-4/3, produce the positive and negative logarithmic singularities. Integrating q/(2h)= derivative of (16/3)log y+(1/3)log(3-y²) cancels cutoff logarithms and yields the stated constant. Independently numerically integrated original discriminant at λ=30,300,1000; renormalized constants respectively 4.8659838551,4.8951958192,4.8957036570 converge to 5+2log(243/256)=4.8957679977. Outer polynomial discriminant reconstructed as [λ²(648+9u⁴-u⁶)+108λ+288-36u²]/9 and the Rayleigh–van-der-Pol map is area preserving (Jacobian determinant ±1); singular scaling and dominated convergence give 60.00037902855485. Small-λ cap is O(λ³) and rationalization yields 13π/243. Finite quadrature supports but does not establish limits.
